Now running the demo itself, clicking the buy button.
---
Ran it myself: clicked the button, the full flow completed in 6.8s. StudyBuddy fetched the card, verified Agent ID #775327772 on-chain, got the 402, checked its policy (0.25 of 1 MMTC cap), settled via the facilitator in 4.4s (payment tx 4GGW7PXH, buyer paid zero fees), and the audit note landed (57CQFINM). Score rendered: 6.5/15, stats ticked to 5 paid reviews, 1.25 MMTC. The machinery genuinely works.

Scores as it stands

Technical use of Algorand: 9. Official @x402/avm, atomic groups, fee pooling, ARC-69 identity, ARC-2 notes, indexer-driven policy. Genuinely good.
x402 / agentic payments: 7. Real 402 round trip with an independent buyer, but the only buyer ever seen is your own StudyBuddy ("1 distinct buyer account"), and the agent card carries no price/accepts block, so buyers must probe to learn the price.
Innovation: 7. The accountability angle is the right idea, but the verify tool only checks the review hash, not the input, so the "prove what it did" claim is half-true right now.
Real-world impact in India: 6. Real pain point, plausible ₹5–10 pricing, but zero validation that the reviews are any good, and the reviewer itself gave an irrelevant example ("Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana" for a mycorrhizae question).
Completeness (demo, repo, video): 4. Demo and repo are strong; the video is a 404 and the DoraHacks submission doesn't exist yet.

Top 6, by score impact

Criterion: all five, literally. Exact change: get the BUIDL actually submitted on DoraHacks. Why: the SUBMISSION_DRAFT says "Not submitted on DoraHacks" over three form questions ("hackathon name", "organising University/Community", "position 1st/2nd/finalist"). None of those require a win; "AlgoBharat", the organiser name, and "participant" answer them honestly. Until this exists, every other fix scores zero.
Criterion: Completeness. Exact change: record and upload the ≤3 min demo.mp4 that the README, SUBMISSION_DRAFT and submission all link to; it 404s right now. Why: video is named in the criterion. Shot list is sitting there: click the button, show the live step timings, open the two explorer txs, run the verify tool. Half an hour of work for a criterion that's currently failing.
Criterion: Completeness, and it actively damages trust. Exact change: the footer "Source on GitHub (MIT)" link points to tab-for-akshay/mainsmarker, which is the old Concordium repo. Point it at mainsmarker-algorand. Why: a judge clicking "Source" lands on a different-chain project with the same name and reasonably concludes the Algorand code isn't what's deployed. This is a one-line fix with outsized downside.
Criterion: Innovation. Exact change: extend "Verify any review" to recompute the input hash (question + answer) alongside the review hash; the ARC-2 note already carries it. Why: as shipped, a judge can paste any review JSON with any audit hash and get "verified"; nothing ties the review to the answer it was paid for. Closing this makes the core claim literally demonstrable in front of judges.
Criterion: Innovation + Impact. Exact change: publish the agent-vs-human table on 10 graded Mains answers in the README (and serve it at an endpoint). Why: the product is the review quality, and right now the same answer scored 7.5, 7.5, then 6.5 with the same model, and 2/10 on another, with no calibration data to say which is right. A small graded table converts "we think it marks well" into evidence.
Criterion: x402 / agentic payments. Exact change: add the x402 accepts block (asset, price 250000, network, feePayer) and the auth-schemes note to the agent card, and make a second, non-self buyer visible, whether that's a one-command scripts/buy.mjs with a faucet-funded account or a public "try it" receipt page. Why: the audit log's "1 distinct buyer" is the classic agentic-commerce tell judges look for; self-trading is a demo, two independent parties is the thesis.

Filing the two new findings so they don't get lost:
